assumptions.choice: Compute each order's size as (1% of initial capital) / current bar's close price (data.close[0]) at signal time
assumptions.reason: Spec states position value must equal 1% of initial capital but does not specify which price to use for the share-count conversion; using the signal bar's close is the most direct literal reading.

assumptions.choice: Use self.broker.startingcash (fixed starting cash) rather than current portfolio value for the 1% sizing calculation
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'initial capital', not current equity, so the base amount should not fluctuate with P&L.

assumptions.choice: Allow at most one averaging (DCA) entry per primary position, gated by an 'averaged' flag reset on exit
assumptions.reason: Spec describes exactly two entry types (primary and 'the second' averaging entry) referencing a single 'entry price of the primary position'; combined with the canonical no-repeated-reentry default, this reads as one additional layer, not unlimited pyramiding while price remains beyond the 1.7% threshold.

assumptions.choice: When both the RSI neutral-zone exit and the 1.7% averaging condition are true on the same bar, the exit takes priority and the averaging entry is skipped
assumptions.reason: Spec gives no ordering; prioritizing exit avoids opening a new position on the same bar the strategy is supposed to be flattening, which is the more conservative/literal reading of 'exiting all positions'.

assumptions.topic: opposite-direction signal while in a position
assumptions.choice: An RSI signal for the opposite side (e.g., RSI>70 while already long) is ignored; only the same-direction averaging entry or the neutral-zone exit can act while a position from the primary signal is open
assumptions.reason: Canonical default: hold at most one position at a time / no re-entry while a position is open, except where the spec explicitly allows the averaging entry; the spec never describes reversing a position on an opposite RSI extreme.

assumptions.choice: Position size is left as a fractional float (1% of capital / price), not rounded to whole shares
assumptions.reason: Spec gives no rounding rule and backtrader supports fractional sizing in backtesting; rounding would introduce an unstated deviation from the exact 1%-of-capital sizing rule.
